info.description: B2B SaaS identity and age verification API. Three route groups: /api/v1 (SDK, API key auth), /dashboard/v1 (dashboard, JWT auth), /admin/v1 (admin panel, JWT + 2FA auth).

get.description: Returns the verification verdict for a session, as the site owner's secret key sees it. `status` is a VERDICT, not a lifecycle marker: `success` means the user PASSED. A session that ran to the end of the flow but missed the age threshold is `failed`, with `reason` explaining why. Possible `status` values: `pending`, `in_progress`, `success`, `failed`, `canceled` (single L), `expired`, `pending_tenant_review`, `awaiting_retake`, `retaken`. Account claiming (Xident ID) does not change the tenant-visible status — a passed verification stays `success` even after a portal account links to it; the internal `claimed` lifecycle state is never returned here. `external_user_id` echoes the `user_id` supplied at init so the session can be correlated to your own user server-side — do not correlate on the browser callback, which is unsigned. Requires a secret API key (sk_live_/sk_test_) — a public key gets 403 SECRET_KEY_REQUIRED. This is the ONE tenant-facing shape: identical regardless of caller, and mirrored verbatim into every webhook's `data` field.

parameters.description: Verification RESULT token (xtk_ prefixed) — NOT the xit_ init token

post.description: Called by the widget after a tenant rejects with reject_mode=retry. Returns a new session token linked to the original; widget restarts capture against it. Enforces max 3 retakes per chain.

409.description: session not in awaiting_retake state OR retake limit exceeded

get.description: Returns the widget-facing verdict for a session — no per-check detail, no age gate, no document/country data, and a masked failure reason (see services.MaskSubjectReason). `status` uses the same public vocabulary as /verify/v1/result/{token}: `pending`, `in_progress`, `success`, `failed`, `canceled` (single L), `expired`, `pending_tenant_review`, `awaiting_retake`, `retaken` — the internal `claimed` lifecycle state (portal account linking) is never returned; a passed verification stays `success`. This is the ONE subject-facing shape: it does not vary by which key type authenticated the request (public or secret both get it), because a credential-dependent response shape is exactly what this endpoint is designed NOT to have.

parameters.description: Verification RESULT token (xtk_ prefixed) — NOT the xit_ init token
parameters.name: token

verification_mode.description:
VerificationMode: "auto" (default) | "document" | "facial".
See models.VerificationMode* for what each enforces.

reason.description:
Reason is masked via MaskSubjectReason — never the raw
VerificationSession.Reason vocabulary.

remaining_attempts.description:
RemainingAttempts is left nil by SubjectResultView. Computing it needs
the API key's configured max-attempts setting (see
verify/sessions_update.go computeRemainingAttempts), which isn't
reachable from a *models.VerificationSession alone — a caller that has
looked up the API key sets this field after calling SubjectResultView.

status.description:
Status carries the same public verdict vocabulary as TenantResult.Status
— see that field's doc comment for the full list and the `claimed`
exclusion/projection rule (publicSessionStatus).

ip_country.description:
IPCountry is where the END USER connected from (IP-derived at session
creation) — a fraud/geo signal for the tenant. Distinct from
checks.document.country, which is the ISSUING country extracted from
the presented document. ADDED 2026-08-04 as the first additive field
after the v1 freeze (announced in the public changelog); additive-only
rules apply — never rename or remove.

status.description:
Status is a VERDICT, uniform across every verification approach
(document, browser check, Xident ID token reuse, and any future path —
e.g. an EU digital wallet) — never an internal lifecycle marker. The
public vocabulary is: pending, in_progress, success, failed, canceled,
expired, pending_tenant_review, awaiting_retake, retaken (see
models/verification_session.go for which of these are named
constants vs. literal values written by the cleanup/retake paths;
note the single-L American spelling of "canceled").
`claimed` is deliberately ABSENT from this list: it is an internal-only
lifecycle state (a portal account linked to an already-passed session)
and is projected to `success` before this struct is built — see
publicSessionStatus. Account claiming (Xident ID) does not change the
tenant-visible status; a passed verification stays `success`.

verification_mode.description:
VerificationMode reports the billing/verification kind this session
resolved to (models.VerificationTypeFull / VerificationTypeToken — a
full document+biometric run vs. a cheap Xident-ID token reuse), sourced
from VerificationSession.VerificationType. It is NOT the request-time
auto/document/facial override (models.VerificationMode*) — that knob
only steers which methods run and isn't itself part of the result.

verified.description:
Verified is the one boolean a tenant should branch on for access
control — derived server-side from Status, never trusted from a client.

reason.description: gyro_unavailable carries a reason string (denied, missing API, …).

ts_ms.description:
Gyro/Light/Visibility events use TsMs (relative to session start).
Latency events use Stage + Ms instead.

capture_luma.description:
CaptureLuma is the brightness (0–255 mean luma) of the ALIGNED FACE CROPS
the client's age model actually ran on — not the whole camera frame, which
reads "well lit" for a user backlit by a window whose face is a silhouette.

Telemetry ONLY: it is logged, never stored, and never affects the verdict.
It exists because the widget currently applies no image-quality gate at all,
so a dark-room verdict is invisible. We log the distribution first and set a
defensible threshold from real data rather than guessing a constant.

gate.description:
Gate is the age bracket the client classified against (== SnapToBracket(min_age)
for a legitimate widget). Optional so older widgets keep working; when present it
must be >= the session's MinAge for the result to count as a pass.

verified.description:
Verified is the client's per-gate classification verdict. Optional for the same
backward-compat reason; when present, only true (plus Gate>=MinAge) is a pass.

expires_in.description:
ExpiresIn is the remaining lifetime of the key in seconds. Widget can
use this to decide when to request a fresh key (most flows complete
well within the TTL so re-fetch is rare).

key.description:
Key is the HMAC key encoded as base64url (unpadded). Widget should
base64url-decode to raw bytes before passing to WebCrypto importKey.

status.description:
The validator tag is a THIRD copy of this vocabulary — after the Go
constants and the SQL — and the only one no compiler or query checks. It
still said "completed" after the rename, so every client PATCH with the
new value was rejected as a validation error before reaching any handler
logic. TestSessionStatusValidatorMatchesTheConstants guards it.

api_key.description:
APIKey is the publishable key for the rest of the phone's calls. It is
released only in exchange for a single-use token, over TLS — never encoded
into the QR image the way it used to be.

methods.description:
Verification context (mirrors what /requirements/check would have returned
for this session, read back from the session row itself).

capture_proof_token.description:
Wave 1.2: optional capture-proof HMAC token emitted by the widget.
Format: base64url(json_payload).hex(HMAC-SHA256(session_key, encoded_payload))
Payload: { "task_id": "<will-match-presign-task>", "capture_mode": "camera", "ts": 1739720400 }
Server verifies in the worker at S3-download time via pkg/captureguard.
Empty when the widget hasn't been upgraded — soft mode applies.

previous.description: original session's xtk_ token (for UI "retrying from..." display)

capture_proof_token.description:
Wave 1.2: capture-proof HMAC token. Widget sends here in addition to
the presign call so the worker can verify without needing a database
round-trip to persist/retrieve the token.

email.description:
Email is deliberately NOT tagged `email` here, only `required`.
Login is a lookup, not a creation gate: any address already in the
accounts table must stay able to sign in. go-playground's `email` rule
is stricter than the address syntax this API has historically accepted
(see isValidEmail below), so tagging it would lock existing users out of
their own accounts. Format is enforced where it belongs — registration.

verification_mode.description:
VerificationMode overrides the rule engine's method choice for THIS
session: "auto" (default), "document" (mandatory ID + face match, no
on-device estimation), or "facial" (on-device only, never a document).

It composes with MinAge rather than replacing it, which is the difference
from Purpose: `purpose: "id_verification"` also forces a document but
zeroes the age threshold, so "show me ID AND require 21" was previously
inexpressible.

outcome.description:
Outcome is what the widget showed the user at the end. It is only ever
"success" or "failed": the widget collapses every non-pass ending into
"failed" before submitting (App.tsx), so a cancel never reaches here.
